decisions.reason: Define-XML ADVS.TRTA names ADSL.TRT01AN, while the reported matched records contain treatment labels in TRTA and dose numbers in that source. The ARM text codelist in the same section suggests a metadata error but does not make the stated copy reproduce the reference.

SAP page-10 defines End of Treatment as the designated Week 24 or early-termination visit, while the vital-sign shell on page-40 defines it as the last on-treatment visit at or before Week 24. These select differently when the last eligible visit is another scheduled visit, and the shell is not stated as an exception to the general definition.

The probe applies the Define-XML ADVS.PCHG "Significant digits: 1" to 100*(CHG/BASE) and differs on rounded versus unrounded quotients, so the documented rule as written does not reproduce the reference. Pilot 6 advs.r L182-L183 computes PCHG with derive_var_pchg() and no later line rounds it, which supports the PCHG__UNROUNDED reading that matches every record.
Define-XML ADVS.STUDYID names ADSL.STUDYID, but advs.yaml STUDYID reads VS.STUDYID. The ADSL1 join supplies other columns and does not change this identifier derivation.
Dataguide page-4 explicitly says STUDYID is merged from ADSL into all analysis datasets, whereas advs.yaml STUDYID reads VS.STUDYID. Matching identifier values do not establish the documented source.
Define-XML ADVS.USUBJID names ADSL.USUBJID, while advs.yaml USUBJID reads VS.USUBJID. Using the identifier to join ADSL1 does not copy its value from that source.
Dataguide page-4 explicitly includes USUBJID among the core variables merged from ADSL, but advs.yaml USUBJID reads VS.USUBJID. This is a source difference even where the keys agree.

Define-XML ADVS.TRTA names ADSL.TRT01AN, but advs.yaml TRTA and its ADSL1 intermediate resolve to ADSL.TRT01A. The ARM text codelist explains the likely intended correction without changing the documented source as written.

SAP page-40 bounds the last on-treatment visit at Week 24, while the complete eot branch in advs.yaml maps Week 26 and ranks every nonmissing mapped visit. Its quoted filter imposes only the lower cutoff and rank, so the documented upper bound has no counterpart.

Native define-sdtm.xml VS.VSBLFL at lines 5035-5044 defines the flag by VISIT="BASELINE". Therefore the BASE1 visit filter expresses the documented baseline condition in Define-XML ADVS.BASE, rather than a different selection rule.

SAP page-13 section 9.2 specifies baseline characteristics for demographic summaries, including height at Visit 1; it does not state the ADVS.BASE lookup rule. Define-XML ADVS.BASE instead explicitly selects VSBLFL="Y", whose native SDTM definition at lines 5035-5044 uses the BASELINE visit, matching BASE1.

SAP page-17 limits the vital-sign endpoint to the last visit on or before Week 24. The complete advs.yaml eot branch can select mapped Week 26, and ANL01FL flags its nonblank endpoint label without restoring that upper bound.

SAP page-40 requires the last on-treatment visit for the vital-sign endpoint. The complete advs.yaml eot branch and ANL01FL contain no treatment-eligibility test; merely outputting TRTSDT and TRTEDT does not apply one.

SAP page-10 names the Week 24 or early-termination visit, while advs.yaml eot ranks all mapped scheduled visits, including Week 26, without identifying an early-termination candidate. ANL01FL then flags every emitted endpoint, so its eligibility does not express that documented definition.

Define-XML ADVS.ABLFL names VS.VSBLFL, but advs.yaml ABLFL reads VS.VISIT in a case expression and never reads the named flag. Native define-sdtm.xml lines 5035-5044 documents the equivalent flag condition, explaining agreement of values without establishing a copy from the documented source.

Define-XML ADVS.ADT states date-part conversion from VS.VSDTC, with no partial-date replacement rule, and the retained section search finds none for vital signs. The explicit date imputations in SAP page-16 and dataguide page-5 concern adverse events and do not support ADT month/day replacement.

Define-XML ADVS.ATPTN says only "Numeric code for ATPT" and does not select VS.VSTPTNUM as its source. Native define-sdtm.xml VS.VSTPTNUM and its codelist document the SDTM codes, but no retained statement binds that coding choice to ADVS.ATPTN.

Define-XML ADVS.ATPTN says only "Numeric code for ATPT", and its native ItemDef at define-adam.xml lines 7228-7235 has no CodeListRef, so no documented numeric coding exists to probe. Pilot 6 advs.r L44-L53 and L141-L143 take ATPTN from that program's own specification codelist, which shows how values were produced but does not document the coding.

SAP page-17 and page-40 explicitly require the last visit, and page-11 assigns vital signs by collected visit labels; descending mapped-visit ranking has that documented last-visit counterpart. The missing Week 24 and on-treatment restrictions are derivation differences, not absence of a documented last-visit operation.

Define-XML ADVS.AVISIT covers observed-visit labels, while SAP page-10 (Week 24 or early termination) and pages 17/40-42 (last on-treatment visit on or before Week 24) give endpoint definitions without an operational candidate, on-treatment or tie rule. Pilot 6 advs.r L157-L168 picks the last record by ADT, AVISITN, ATPTN and AVAL among AVISITN > 2, a choice no retained document states.

Define-XML ADVS.BASE states the flagged VS.VSSTRESN lookup, the ADVS ItemGroupDef at define-adam.xml lines 3303-3304 fixes the subject/parameter/timepoint keys, native VS.VSBLFL at define-sdtm.xml lines 5035-5044 flags the BASELINE visit, and native lines 15387-15438 give the parameter-level types. Leaving that retained metadata out of the section adapter does not make the documented rule incomplete; Pilot 6 advs.r L176-L180 groups by the same keys.

Define-XML ADVS.CHG states the complete AVAL-BASE arithmetic, and native define-adam.xml lines 15439-15490 give the parameter-level integer or one-decimal types, so the rule is not incomplete; its omission from the section adapter is an interface limitation. Pilot 6 advs.r L182 computes CHG with derive_var_chg() and no rounding, consistent with that arithmetic.

The advs.yaml eot filter requires _SRC_AVISITN > 2 before its endpoint receives ANL01FL="Y". SAP page-10, page-17 and pages 40-42 state the endpoint visit criteria without this strict after-Week-2 cutoff, and no retained section supplies it.

Define-XML ADVS.ANL01FL gives the flag meaning and excluded source visits but not whether derived End of Treatment records or repeated assessments are flagged, and SAP page-10 and pages 17/40-42 leave the endpoint selection unresolved. Pilot 6 advs.r L186-L192 flags every record with nonmissing AVISIT, including each added End of Treatment record, a choice no retained document states.

missed.quote:
Demographic data for screen failures will be 
included in the data tabulation datasets, but not in the analysis 
datasets or in the analyses.
missed.reason: SAP section 6 supplies this uncited screen-failure exclusion statement for analysis records carrying demographics. It belongs to the base row scope, not an analysis-flag derivation.
